methodology.prior_formulation: Bayesian with NEA Baseline (97% Marine / 3% Inland) + Dynamic IFI Coupling

attribution_reports.hotspot_name: East Coast Shoreline & Bedok Waters Hotspot #1

breakdown.description: Commercial maritime traffic, container transshipment anchorage zones, and offshore vessel discard along the Traffic Separation Scheme (TSS).
Urban stormwater runoff, canal drainage flushes, and crest gate discharges (Marina Barrage, Kallang River, Jurong River).
Regional transboundary ocean currents entering Singapore waters from the Riau Archipelago, Batam, and Bintan straits.
Cross-border estuarine and river discharge from Sungei Skudai, Sungei Tebrau, and Johor River flushing through the Johor Strait.
Direct shoreline recreation, beach visitors, park littering, and nearshore activities along public beaches (ECP, Sentosa, Pasir Ris).

attribution_reports.operational_narrative: Lagrangian reverse advection (-29.8h) indicates high attribution confidence to Singapore Strait Shipping Channel (91.9% posterior probability). Secondary influence from Local Inland Waterways & Canals (4.3%). Overall split: 95.6% Marine/Transboundary vs. 4.4% Inland/Shoreline. Dry weather conditions prevail; inland runoff minimal, aligning with NEA baseline marine dominance (97%).
